# repo-map.yaml — the map of this monorepo.
#
# This file is the entry point for any agent or person working in the repo.
# Read it first, find the part you have been assigned, and read only the
# directories listed under that part's `path` and under the `path` of each
# part it depends on. You should not need to read anything else.
#
# Invariants (keep these true when you edit this file):
#   - Every `id` under `parts` and `apps` is unique.
#   - Every entry in a part's `present_in` is an `id` under `apps`.
#   - Every entry in a part's `depends_on` is an `id` under `parts`.
#   - `depends_on` is a direct dependency only; it is not transitive and it
#     must not contain cycles.
#   - If part A depends on part B, then A's `present_in` must be a subset of
#     B's `present_in` — a part cannot be present in an app its dependency
#     is absent from.
#   - Adding, moving, or deleting a part is not done until this file says so.

schema: repo-map/v1

# The deployable applications in the monorepo. A "part" is present in zero or
# more of these; an app is built from the parts that name it in `present_in`.
apps:
  - id: web
    path: apps/web
    description: Customer-facing web application.

  - id: mobile
    path: apps/mobile
    description: iOS and Android application, React Native.

# The parts of the product. One part = one owned slice of the repo = the unit
# of work handed to a single agent.
parts:
  - id: core-auth
    path: packages/core-auth
    purpose: >-
      Identity, sessions, and token refresh. Owns the user and session models
      and the only code that talks to the auth provider.
    depends_on: []
    present_in:
      - web
      - mobile

  - id: ui-account
    path: packages/ui-account
    purpose: >-
      Sign-in, sign-up, and account settings screens. Renders the flows that
      core-auth backs; holds no auth logic of its own.
    depends_on:
      - core-auth
    present_in:
      - web
      - mobile

  - id: mobile-push
    path: packages/mobile-push
    purpose: >-
      Device registration and push notification delivery. Depends on native
      APNs and FCM modules, so it ships in the mobile app only.
    depends_on: []
    present_in:
      - mobile
```

# REPO-MAP.yaml
#
# The one file every agent reads before touching this repository.
# It answers three questions, and deliberately nothing else:
#
#   1. What are the parts?        -> parts.<id>.summary and parts.<id>.path
#   2. What depends on what?      -> parts.<id>.depends_on
#   3. Where does each part ship? -> parts.<id>.present_in
#
# HOW TO USE THIS AS AN AGENT
#   Find your part by its id. Your reading slice is:
#     - everything under your own `path`, plus
#     - the `api` file of each part in your `depends_on` (transitively).
#   You do not need to read the implementation of your dependencies, and you do
#   not need to read parts that are not in your transitive `depends_on`.
#
# RULES THAT KEEP THIS FILE TRUE
#   - `depends_on` lists direct dependencies only, and lists all of them.
#     If you add an import across a part boundary, add the edge here in the
#     same change.
#   - The graph must stay acyclic.
#   - Containment: a part's `present_in` must be a subset of the `present_in`
#     of every part it depends on. A part cannot ship somewhere its
#     dependencies do not.
#   - Only cross the boundary through a part's `api` file. Reaching into a
#     dependency's internals is a bug even when the language allows it.
#   - Edit only the entry for the part you are working on. Concurrent agents
#     touching separate entries should never conflict here.

schema_version: 1

# The deployable applications. `present_in` values must be keys of this map.
apps:
  web:
    path: apps/web
    summary: Customer-facing storefront and account area.
  admin:
    path: apps/admin
    summary: Internal back-office console used by the support team.

# The parts. Keyed by id so an agent can look up its own slice directly.
parts:

  money:
    path: packages/money
    summary: >
      Currency, amount, and rounding value types. Pure computation, no I/O and
      no framework imports. The shared vocabulary for anything that touches a
      price.
    api: packages/money/src/index.ts
    depends_on: []
    present_in: [web, admin]

  billing-core:
    path: packages/billing-core
    summary: >
      Subscription plans, proration, and invoice construction. Owns the billing
      state machine and the rules for what a customer is charged. Talks to the
      payment provider behind its own interface.
    api: packages/billing-core/src/index.ts
    depends_on: [money]
    present_in: [web, admin]

  admin-audit-log:
    path: packages/admin-audit-log
    summary: >
      Append-only record of back-office actions, including manual invoice
      adjustments, with the operator identity attached. Never exposed to
      customers, which is why it ships in the admin app only.
    api: packages/admin-audit-log/src/index.ts
    depends_on: [billing-core]
    present_in: [admin]
```

The example is internally consistent with the containment rule: `admin-audit-log` ships only to `admin`, and both parts it depends on (directly and transitively) ship to a superset of that.

I chose YAML because this file's audience is agents reading it as plain text, and YAML carries the explanatory comments — the usage protocol and the invariants — in the same file as the data, which JSON cannot do. Keying `parts` by id rather than using a list means an agent can find its own entry and its dependencies' entries by name without scanning the whole structure, which is the same "read a small slice" property you want from the repo itself. The line-oriented syntax also matters with several agents committing at once: adding a part is a pure block insertion with no trailing commas or closing braces to fight over, so two agents editing different entries produce clean merges. I kept it to five fields per part so that keeping it accurate stays cheap enough that agents actually will.

#
# An agent working on one part should be able to read this file plus its own
# part's directory, and nothing else.
#
# Reading protocol for agents:
#   1. Find your part in `parts` by `id`.
#   2. Read everything under its `path`.
#   3. For each id in its `depends_on`, read only that part's `public_api` file.
#      Do not read the rest of a dependency's implementation.
#   4. Do not import from, or edit, a part that is not in your `depends_on`.
#

#   - Every id in `depends_on` exists in `parts`; every id in `present_in`
#     exists in `apps`.
#   - `depends_on` is acyclic.
#   - If part A depends on part B, every app in A.present_in is also in
#     B.present_in.

schema_version: 1

apps:
  - id: web
    path: apps/web
    purpose: Customer-facing application.

  - id: admin
    path: apps/admin
    purpose: Internal operator console.

  - id: ui-primitives

    purpose: Checkout flow and invoice screens.
    public_api: packages/billing-ui/src/index.ts
